ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of beneficial owners (RBE Law); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 30 January 2019 implementing the RBE Law; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS Law); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended) for partnership forms; Law of 11 January 2019 implementing EU Directive 2017/1132 (company law digitalisation).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Partnership agreement or constitutive instrument (contrat de société) of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partner(s) and limited partner(s), executed in writing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if any document originates from a non-Luxembourg jurisdiction party to the 1961 Hague Convention) OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague signatory jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate existence for each corporate partner (statutory representative and registered agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry in the partner's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity documents (passport or national ID) of the general partner’s legal representative, ultimate beneficial owners, and any signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / competent national ID issuer of the individual's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy by Luxembourg notary or consular officer, then legalization/apostille as applicable; certified translation into French/German/Luxembourgish if not already in an official language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered address location (lease agreement, service agreement, or administrative agent confirmation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Lessor or Luxembourg-based corporate services provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (for foreign-issued title deeds); local Luxembourg notary certification for domestic address leases

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or source-of-funds declaration covering initial contribution and expected capital flows
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the contributing shareholder / partner or the account-holding financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for foreign bank letters; Luxembourg notary attestation for domestic bank letters

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all direct and ultimate beneficial owners, general partners, authorized signatories, and counterparties against (i) Luxembourg domestic financial sanctions list issued by the Ministry of Finance; (ii) the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) administrative freezing orders; (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EU CFSP); (iv) OFAC SDN List for USD-related activities; (v) UN Security Council Consolidated List; and (vi) FATF high-risk and non-cooperative jurisdictions. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, high-risk third countries, and any transaction chain where documentary explanation is inconsistent. Protocols include risk scoring, continuous monitoring, adverse media checks, and mandatory suspicious transaction reporting to the Luxembourg FIU (CRF) under Article 5 and Chapter 4 of the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via LBR online portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Applications may be submitted in French, German, or Luxembourgish. The registered name must be written in Latin script and be clearly pronounceable; foreign-language names are permitted but must include a transliteration into the Luxembourgish/French/German phonetic rules for registration. The mandatory legal suffix 'SCSp' (or full form 'Société en Commandite Spéciale') must appear at the end of the name. Names must not be contrary to public order, must not mislead the public, and must respect the rules against deceptive trade descriptions. For cosplay and prop apparel manufacturing, the name may reference 'Cosplay', 'Costume', 'Props', or similar nouns without ministerial approval, provided the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS entry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a formal refusal with grounds. Within fifteen (15) days from notification, the applicant (directly or through a Luxembourg lawyer/company formation agent) may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of the Luxembourg Business Registers, setting out the legal basis and evidence of name availability. The Registrar must rule within one (1) month. If unsatisfied, the applicant may further appeal to the First Instance District Court (Tribunal d’arrondissement de Luxembourg) under Article 26 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial registers, with a request for an injunction to order registration. The name reservation window of 30 days is not automatically extended pending appeal; a fresh name request must be filed if the appeal process exceeds the reservation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual or registered-agent-only office is not sufficient for RCS purposes. Luxembourg law requires a fixed physical Luxembourg address where legal correspondence, service of process, and statutory documents can be received and where the administrative records are kept. For an SCSp engaged in cosplay costume and synthetic wig retail manufacturing without regulated status, a compliant administrative agent office with physical reception and filing capability is permitted; however, complete absence of any physical presence or the use of a mere letterbox without contractual substance is disfavoured and may be challenged under Luxembourg general anti-abuse rules and the economic substance expectations in BEPS and anti-fragmentation policies.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate — approximately 8-12% per operational year for a standard non-regulated SCSp in retail manufacturing, rising to up to 30% if the partnership carries a high-volume turnover in e-commerce, has unexplained fund flows, or operates in a sector flagged by the Luxembourg FIU. Random administrative verifications are performed under Article 35 of the RBE Law and Article 5 of the RCS Law.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official LBR tariff for name clearance / preliminary search (statutory cap, no separate fee for first search, small token fee for advanced conflict checks).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS formal incorporation filing fee for Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory registration tariff under Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 July 2016 (as amended); fee varies with number of partners and length of constitutive deed.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the SCSp constitutive act and registration extract in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Central Luxembourg Information and Press Service / Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat statutory publication fee determined by the Ministry of Justice for electronic publication in the RESA journal.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of beneficial owners in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE, Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), acting as RBE administrator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official LBR tariff for UBO declaration filing (€30 per entity, translated at market rate into USD).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization fees for foreign partner corporate documents and evidence (estimated two documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority in partner's home country (Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Apostille office or Consulate)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention per-document fee, typically USD 45-85 per apostille; consular legalization ranges from USD 60-120 per document depending on jurisdiction.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation fees for the constitutive agreement and corporate documents into French or German (if applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation service provider (Luxembourg or foreign) or Luxembourg notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for professional legal translation, USD 0.20-0.40 per word including notarised certificate of translation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fee for optional notarization of the partnership agreement (only if the parties elect to notarize to facilitate third-party signature or financing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notary tariff under the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 and the notarial fee schedule of the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg; optional service.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence review and drafting of the SCSp partnership agreement, AML/KYC bundle, and UBO declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / registered formation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for a non-regulated SCSp formation with AML/KYC compliance; fixed fee range USD 1,500-2,500 in the current Luxembourg market.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales, as amended — Articles 101-1 et seq. (Société en Commandite Spéciale introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013); Loi du 19 décembre 2002 sur le registre de commerce et des sociétés
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 2, Avenue John F. Kennedy, L-1855 Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / contrat de société (partnership agreement) plus the standard RCS registration form submitted electronically via lbr.lu
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital applicable to an SCSp; contributions are free as agreed in the partnership agreement; no escrow account or bank capital block certificate is legally required, though a proof-of-contribution bank reference is customary
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the sole general partner of LU_SCSP, acting at a duly convened meeting held in Luxembourg on [date], that: (1) the subscriptions to partnership interests in the Société en Commandite Spéciale are hereby ratified and accepted; (2) the registered office of the partnership is established at [address], Luxembourg, and the manager is authorised to execute the lease and obtain required municipal consents; (3) [Name] is appointed statutory manager (gérant) with sole signatory authority; (4) management is authorised to open bank accounts, complete RCS registration, and file declarations with the ACD, AEDT and CCSS; and (5) all acts performed previously in the partnership's name are ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS online extract service (lbr.lu) and Institut de la Propriété Intellectelle Luxembourg (IPIL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online search against the RCS central index to confirm that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company; verify trademark conflicts with IPIL; because formal name reservation is not available, obtain written provisional clearance from the drafting notary or counsel before executing the deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (plus two alternates)
Short description of the activity (ISIC 3240)
Identification details of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity, select a new distinctive name with a differentiating element (e.g., a trademark suffix), obtain fresh LBR clearance, and amend the draft partnership agreement before signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Signing of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (required where real property is contributed) or private writing signed by all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the contrat de société / partnership agreement in French or English; define the roles of the general partner (commandité) and limited partner(s) (commanditaire), capital contributions, profit-sharing, management powers, and economic substance provisions; obtain notarial authentication where required and complete AML/KYC verification for all partners and beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Final draft partnership agreement
AML/KYC file of each partner (passport, proof of address, source of funds)
Certificate of good standing of any corporate general partner
Bank reference or proof of contribution to capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries KYC documents or name clearance, furnish supplementary bank references or revise the offending clauses; any material defect is cured by restating and re-executing the deed before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers online portal (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the deed, submit the standard RCS registration form electronically using Luxembourg eID or LCSS authentication; disclose the manager, partners, registered office, and contribution amounts; pay the EUR 75 filing fee electronically; the RCS registration automatically triggers publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations) official gazette.
required_dossiers: Original notarial or private partnership deed
Completed RCS standard registration form for partnerships
Statement of registered office address with lease or letter of consent
Copy of the manager's national identity document
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a rectification notice, respond in writing within the prescribed period (generally one month); missing annexes may be re-submitted online without reopening the file; late registration may expose the manager to a court-imposed fine, so immediate corrective filing is advised.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the ACD automatically allocates the national taxpayer number (matricule); apply to the AEDT for a VAT identification number via the LCSS portail if annual taxable turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 or if voluntary VAT registration is desired for input VAT recovery; register any employees with the CCSS within 8 days of their start date.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Certified copy of the partnership agreement
Proof of registered office address
Bank account details
Identification documents of managers and partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT fails to issue a VAT number within two weeks, file a follow-up request via Guichet.lu or attend the AEDT counter; invoice only after VAT registration is confirmed, as premature VAT invoicing may attract penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Electronic Access Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or payment institution supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an operating account in the name of LU_SCSP; provide the RCS extract, deed, and beneficial owner declarations; complete the bank's KYC questionnaire; activate Luxembourg eID/LCSS digital credentials for future online administrative procedures; confirm that the intended payment rails (Stripe, Shopify Payments) can be linked via the acquiring bank or an approved payment service provider.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the partnership deed
RCS registration extract and VAT number
Beneficial ownership register / AML declaration form
Identity documents of partners and ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's AML committee requests further information, provide transaction-level source-of-funds documentation; if the initial bank declines, approach an alternate CSSF-licensed bank or a specialized payment institution; maintain records in English or French to expedite review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Commencement Notification and Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet.lu (single point of contact), municipal administration of the Commune de Luxembourg, and Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Declare the commencement of business and the physical workshop premises through Guichet.lu; verify with the municipal zoning authority that the workshop address permits light manufacturing (ISIC 3240); since the activity is not a regulated profession, no separate autorisation d'établissement is required, but the business declaration is mandatory; if employees are hired, schedule an ITM workplace inspection and obtain the required occupational safety clearance.
required_dossiers: Declaration of activity form (Formulaire de déclaration d'activité)
Registered office lease or proof of premises title
RCS registration extract
Landlord's written consent for workshop use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality opposes the workshop on zoning grounds, apply for a zoning derogation or relocate the activity to a permitted mixed-use industrial zone; any ITM enforcement order is cured by implementing corrective safety measures and passing a follow-up inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie — Direction de l'industrie (industrial policy oversight); municipal zoning authority at the Commune de Luxembourg
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no sectoral industrial operating licence is required for ISIC 3240 (manufacture of costume props and theatrical apparel) under Luxembourg law; only a standard business commencement declaration via Guichet.lu is mandatory

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA under the Loi du 15 mai 2018 sur l'évaluation environnementale for light apparel and toy manufacturing below Annex II thresholds; a simple environmental registration or pre-notification may apply if wastewater or waste outputs exceed municipal de minimis limits
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 May 2016 and EU Directive 2010/75/EU (IED) where relevant; volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from coatings and adhesives are capped under EU Directive 2004/42/EC; textile waste and production residues must be handled and recorded pursuant to the Loi du 21 mars 2017 relative à la gestion des déchets

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification of the workshop by the Administration des services de secours (CGDIS); structural load inspection and occupancy permit from the municipal building authority; workplace health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including ventilation, electrical safety, and ergonomic assessments before employee deployment

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des Contributions Directes - ACD) for direct taxes; Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA - AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for business and beneficial-owner registration; electronic portal: MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SCSp partnership deed before a Luxembourg notary and file statutory particulars with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), obtaining the national business registration number (numéro de matricule) and completing the beneficial-owner filing with the Register of Beneficial Owners. Step 2: File VAT registration Form 640 with the AEDT, using the LBR matricule, supported by the partnership deed, proof of economic activity, identity documents of general and limited partners and, for non-EU principals, evidence of appointment of a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative. Step 3: Receive the Luxembourg VAT identification number and, where applicable, activate VIES registration for intra-Community transactions. The SCSp is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes and does not itself file corporate income tax, municipal business tax or net wealth tax; each partner is taxed directly on the distributive share, but the SCSp remains a separate VAT registrant and taxable person.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: the SCSp has no separate legal personality under Luxembourg law and is income-tax transparent by default; it is not subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax or net wealth tax, and partners are taxed directly on their distributive shares. For indirect tax purposes, however, the SCSp constitutes a separate taxable person and must account for Luxembourg VAT on taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg operates no US-style check-the-box regime. Article 175bis(2) of the Income Tax Law permits an eligible commercial partnership to elect corporate taxation where all partners are corporate entities subject to an equivalent corporate income tax. EU ATAD hybrid mismatch rules require the Luxembourg classification of the SCSp to be aligned with that of foreign partner jurisdictions, and mismatches are neutralised through denial of deduction or inclusion under the 2020 implementing legislation. For VAT, the SCSp may waive the small-business franchise exemption (EUR 35,000 threshold) and may elect the Import One Stop Shop (IOSS) scheme for distance sales of imported goods not exceeding EUR 150 in value.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover ceiling for the small-business franchise exemption for Luxembourg-established businesses; VAT registration is mandatory once annual turnover exceeds this threshold. Non-established suppliers have no threshold and must register from their first taxable supply in Luxembourg. For intra-Community distance sales of goods to Luxembourg consumers, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual distance-sales threshold applies; the IOSS covers distance sales of imported goods not exceeding EUR 150.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time continuous transaction control (CTC) e-invoicing, government API clearance or digital stamping system for B2B/B2C invoices. Mandatory PEPPOL-based electronic invoicing applies only to public procurement (B2G) under the Law of 17 March 2023, using the EN 16931 semantic data model. VAT returns and EC Sales Lists must be filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu; the AEDT may require SAF-T XML files from large taxpayers during audits. Luxembourg participates in the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) initiative for future e-invoicing and digital reporting mandates.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 54 of the Luxembourg VAT Act zero-rates supplies of goods physically exported to a non-EU destination and supplies of goods transported to EU VAT-registered customers as intra-Community supplies, subject to documentary conditions. The goods must leave the EU in the condition in which they were supplied; the supplier or the purchaser must furnish a valid customs export declaration; and transport, invoice and payment records must evidence delivery to a non-EU address. Services directly connected with the export of goods, such as freight, handling, customs clearance and transit storage for export, may also be zero-rated. E-commerce cosplay-prop apparel sales processed via Stripe and Shopify Payments qualify for zero-rating where each parcel is dispatched to a non-EU consumer and is covered by an accepted electronic export declaration at the Luxembourg or other EU customs office of exit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: Single Administrative Document (SAD) or electronic export declaration (ECS) accepted by the EU customs office of exit, showing the 8-digit commodity code, gross weight, and non-EU destination country
Transport proof of physical removal: signed CMR consignment note, Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or express/postal carrier consignment record with non-EU delivery confirmation
Commercial invoice with incoterms, unit values, harmonised commodity codes, and identity of the non-EU buyer/payee
Inward foreign-currency remittance certificate, SWIFT or bank payment confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-EU customer
VEIES/EC Sales List confirmation and customer VAT registration number where the supply qualifies as an intra-Community B2B sale
EUR.1/EUR-MED movement certificate or origin declaration where preferential tariff origin is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg Customs may retrospectively reassess VAT for up to five years, or ten years in fraud cases, and claw back zero-rated treatment where the export documentation bundle is incomplete, goods are diverted into EU consumption, or export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory deadline. Administrative penalties for incorrect VAT returns begin at 10% of the tax underdeclared, increase to 50% for deliberate concealment, and may reach 100% for serious fraud; late-payment interest accrues at 0.8% per month on the outstanding VAT. Criminal sanctions for fraudulent export zero-rating include fines up to EUR 75,000 and imprisonment for responsible partners and managers, and joint and several liability applies to participants in VAT evasion chains involving fictitious export invoices or intermediary shell entities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the banking supervisory and AML/CTF control authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full Eurozone member and maintains no foreign exchange control regime; the euro is freely convertible across both current and capital account transactions pursuant to Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Council Directive 88/361/EEC. Profit remittance and capital repatriation for a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) are unrestricted; because the SCSp is tax-transparent, income and gains flow directly to limited partners per the partnership agreement without entity-level repatriation hurdles. The only practical barriers are documentary: AML/KYC confirmation of beneficial owners, registration of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), and balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the BCL under EU Regulation 184/2005. No licensing, approval, or conversion mandate applies to capital movements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no timeline for repatriating export proceeds. Export receipts denominated in USD or other foreign currencies may be retained in correspondent accounts, converted to EUR at commercial discretion, or used for trade disbursements without central bank authorization. Reporting obligations are limited to threshold-based balance-of-payments statistics filed with the BCL under EU Regulation 184/2005 and CSSF guidance, which carry no restrictive effect on liquidity management.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Trade Finance Facility
Operational Account / Documentary Credit and Guarantee Facility
Private and Institutional Operational Account / Custody Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / FX Hedging Desk
Operational Account for Private Wealth-linked Partnership Structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as an ancillary liquidity channel; Low-Medium as a primary treasury or capital escrow venue. Licensed Luxembourg or EEA-passported Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Revolut Business, and Airwallex, operating under PSD2 with CSSF or home-state regulatory oversight, can provide rapid euro IBANs, marketplace collection settlement for Stripe/Shopify payouts, and lower-cost cross-border payments. However, they are not a substitute for tier-1 Luxembourg commercial banks: EMI sub-account architecture rarely accommodates capital escrow, blocked accounts, statutory auditor confirmations, commercial LC issuance, or credit lines; they also present concentration risk and are often unwilling to serve pass-through partnerships with non-resident UBOs due to internal risk appetite. Optimal structure is a cluster of EMI transaction accounts for e-commerce receipts and working capital, swept daily to a BIL or Spuerkeess operational account, with all equity subscriptions and profit distributions channeled exclusively through the regulated Luxembourg banking sector.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Direct physical presence of the SCSp's general partner signatories is the prevailing expectation for a first-time onboarding at most Luxembourg tier-1 banks, including BIL, Banque de Luxembourg, and Société Générale Luxembourg. Luxembourg AML law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended) does not per se require a face-to-face interview, provided the bank can complete an equivalent remote identification via secure video identification, eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures, and notarized or apostilled corporate documents. In practice, a hybrid mandate applies: the general partner (or an authorized local agent) must attend at least one in-person or high-assurance video meeting at the bank premises, while limited partners may complete remote KYC with certified passport copies, proof of address, and source-of-wealth files. Foreign signatory entities established outside the EU should expect legalization chain requirements (apostille plus, in some cases, notarized translation) and a personality verification call with compliance officers before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through SCSp structure with non-resident limited partners and an opaque commercial chain between the partnership, marketplaces, and Asian garment suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the SCSp partnership agreement and deed; Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) filing confirmation; full LP/GP register; corporate diagram showing each UBO; passport copies, residential proof, CV/organigram of every beneficial owner; source-of-wealth statement of each LP; Luxembourg tax counsel legal opinion confirming pass-through classification and economic substance; annual financial statements of the SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mortgage-like ambiguity in business scope: ISIC 3240 / cosplay prop and theatrical apparel manufacturing is a niche e-commerce segment with no statutory licensing, creating uncertainty as to the authenticity and legitimacy of commercial revenues.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan and operating model description; executed merchant service agreements with Stripe and Shopify Payments; historical payout and settlement statements from marketplaces; representative purchase orders, invoices, and proof of delivery; illustrated bill of materials from licensed suppliers of synthetic wigs and costume fabrics; customs import/export declarations and logistics waybill files; Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce excerpt confirming business purpose; CSSF confirmation or legal opinion that no Luxembourg financial or gaming license is triggered by the activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket e-commerce receipts across multiple jurisdictions, raising potential concerns around layering, chargebacks, and unidentified counterparties on Stripe/Shopify rails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant account structure and KYC documents for the legal entity; order-to-cash workflow narrative; chargeback ratio report and refund policy; customer identification mechanism; reconciliation file mapping each marketplace payout to underlying sales; country-wise sales breakdown; VAT registration certificates (including EU OSS and, where relevant, import IOSS); e-commerce platform terms and data-processing addendum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injections from non-EU limited partners and sizable USD-denominated trade payments to textile and wig manufacturers, which may appear as unusually structured flows or be misread as evidence of trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription agreement and capital call notices for each LP; bank statements evidencing the source of funds at LP level; personal/branch balance sheets of contributing partners; remittance instructions referencing the SCSp subordinated loan/equity purpose code; audit trail of downstream payments to manufacturers; purchase contracts, letters of credit, and pro-forma invoices demonstrating genuine underlying trade; insurance certificates on shipped goods; confirmation that disbursements are made only to pre-approved beneficiary lists held by the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections follow a strict documented chain: (1) capital call notice issued by the SCSp general partner in accordance with the partnership agreement; (2) each limited partner initiates a wire transfer from their own bank account via SWIFT MT103 with the payment narrative clearly referencing the SCSp name and the purpose 'Capital Contribution – SCSp Subscription'; (3) for EUR contributions, settlement occurs via TARGET2 through the BCL or via the pan-European ACH/SEPA Instant Credit scheme for smaller amounts; for USD contributions, settlement occurs via CHIPS or Fedwire through the bank's US correspondent using the same MT103 narrative; (4) the receiving Luxembourg bank performs sanctions/PEP screening, verifies the remitter against the registered UBO list, and credits the capital escrow sub-account, where amounts remain blocked pending delivery of contribution documentation and the standard notarized/legalized certificate of registration; (5) simultaneous balance-of-payments statistical coding is filed to the BCL under direct investment/equity capital categories. No central bank approval is required, but banks will reject injections missing the SCSp-beneficiary designation or sourced from third-party pass-through accounts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for cosplay prop apparel, theatrical costume fabrics, and synthetic wigs are cleared through multi-rail architecture. For EU and EEA suppliers: SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit via EBA CLEARING. For non-EU cross-border euro payments: SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) with remittance details referencing the underlying invoice and PO number. For large USD purchases, typically from Asian textile manufacturers: commercial letters of credit issued by the Luxembourg relationship bank under UCP600, with SWIFT MT700 transmission and MT202/MT202COV cover payment instructions; documentary collections (CAD basis) for mid-value shipments; and bank-to-bank MT103 direct transfers for repeat suppliers after credit approval. The treasury desk should maintain separate beneficiary account lists per supplier, hard-checked against invoices and shipping documents, to satisfy bank transaction-monitoring expectations. Any disbursement above a pre-agreed threshold requires dual authorization by the general partner and an independent co-signatory or authorized compliance officer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward (Outright) – EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNH forwards for firm settlement of export receipts and supplier payables
FX Swap (Rollover) – for temporary EUR/USD liquidity restructuring without immediate balance-sheet impact
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) – for restricted or thin-market currencies linked to final buyer jurisdictions outside the EU/OCED convertibility sphere
Cross-Currency Swap (Fixed/Floating) – long-term USD liability restructuring aligned with licensed costume IP procurement contracts
Vanilla FX Options (Call/Put) – off-market-protected hedging for competitive tender and e-commerce price-list exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered company data (confirmation annuelle RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés via e-Desktop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following each anniversary of the SCSp's RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: LBR reminder after expiry; continued default triggers a court summons, monetary penalties, and ultimately administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts of the SCSp (comptes annuels) - abridged balance sheet permitted for small undertakings; filed with RCS and published in RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (electronic deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by the general partner/partners within 6 months of the financial year-end; deposit with RCS within 1 month of approval; effective hard deadline of 7 months after year-end (31 July for a 31 December financial year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit results in court summons and civil penalties; repeated non-filing for consecutive years exposes the SCSp to judicial dissolution and administrative radiation from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial-owner data in the RBE register; amendment filings where ownership changes occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) via e-file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due by 31 March of each calendar year; any qualifying change in direct or indirect beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 125,000 (approximately US$136,000), publication of sanctions, and criminal penalties for intentional non-disclosure or false declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership tax return (Form 545) incorporating the municipal business tax (ICC) declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg direct tax office with territorial competence for the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due by 30 June of the year following the calendar tax year; ACD e-file practice commonly extends the deadline to 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Taxation d'office, default interest of 0.6% per month, penalty surcharge of up to 10% of assessed tax, and criminal fines for deliberate non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual economic survey response (enquête annuelle économique) collected by STATEC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: STATEC - Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within the response window stated in the annual questionnaire, generally February to April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Written reminder from STATEC; persistent non-response is subject to administrative fines under the Luxembourg official statistics law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé is compulsory when the SCSp exceeds at least two of the three large-undertaking thresholds: balance-sheet total over EUR 20 million, net turnover over EUR 40 million, or average staff over 250. The SCSp is exempt from audit as a small undertaking when it does not exceed at least two of: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, or average staff 50; the partnership agreement may nevertheless impose an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts of undertakings; statutory accounts prepared in euro; IFRS voluntary option permitted for the statutory annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must confirm the identity, nature, and extent of beneficial ownership of all ultimate beneficial owners by 31 March of each calendar year through the RBE electronic portal; any transfer of partnership interests that modifies control or ownership percentages must be declared within 30 days, with supporting evidence retained for AML/CFT inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (ownership schedule mirroring the SCSp agreement and transfer ledger)
Minute Book of partner and general-partner resolutions
RBE beneficial-owner register file (copy of the filed RBE declaration maintained at the Luxembourg office)
Accounting books, ledgers, and supporting vouchers subject to the 10-year retention rule

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,700 - 3,900 (EUR 1,500 - 3,500) per annum for a Luxembourg registered office, AML verification, and registered agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,500 - 16,500 (EUR 5,000 - 15,000) per audit cycle where a statutory audit is triggered; most small SCSp are audit-exempt and incur only bookkeeping or voluntary review fees

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined in Luxembourg City for a taxable corporate entity (CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% of CIT + municipal business tax 6.75%); a transparent SCSp is not subject to CIT at entity level and this rate applies only to the taxable partners
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No classic statutory tax holiday. Luxembourg offers an IP box regime granting an 80% exemption on net qualifying IP royalty income, reducing the combined 24.94% headline rate to an effective 4.99% for qualifying licensed costume IP and synthetic-wig patents; the participation exemption fully exempts qualifying dividends and capital gains; investment tax credits of 8% on qualifying fixed assets and R&D credits further reduce effective taxation at the partner level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (IRC - Corporate Income Tax Return) for each partner; filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu / ACD e-space using LuxTrust authentication. A transparent SCSp itself does not file Form 100 because its income is allocated to partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than five months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 May for a 31 December year-end), unless an extension to 30 June or a later date is obtained from the ACD; professional advisers routinely request extensions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner identification, tax number, registered address, fiscal year-end, percentage share in the SCSp, and designation of the Luxembourg permanent establishment if the SCSp physically manufactures in Luxembourg.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner must state the Luxembourg business address and appoint a local fiscal representative for service of tax assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable commercial profit after commercial-accounting adjustments, including all revenue from tailoring licensed theatrical costume robes, synthetic wigs, and cosplay prop apparel sold via Stripe and Shopify Payments, less deductible operating expenses and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the share of profit attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment is reported; foreign e-commerce sales that are not connected with the Luxembourg PE are excluded from Luxembourg taxation unless sourced by a taxable presence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner-level deductions including IP box exemption of 80% of net income from qualifying IP, participation exemption on dividends received, investment tax credit, and any treaty deductions claimed by the partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty relief is claimed in the partner's residence tax return; if a tax treaty assigns the SCSp profit to the partner's residence, a certificate of residency and a detailed partnership allocation statement must be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the SCSp's net taxable income between general and limited partners according to the partnership agreement, including performance allocations and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure the allocation is supported by the deed and the audited accounts; improper allocations may be recharacterized as constructive dividends or taxable profit distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted partner filings may lead to ex officio assessment, administrative fines up to EUR 10,000, default interest of 0.6% per month on the underpaid tax, and, in cases of intentional fraud, criminal tax penalties.
